arrets.Étoile Rouge: The big junction where five roads meet, around the Red Star monument.
arrets.Dantokpa: The largest open-air market in West Africa, on the edge of the lagoon.
arrets.Missèbo: The fabric and second-hand clothes market, just south of Dantokpa.
arrets.Zongo: The neighbourhood of the great mosque with its two white minarets.
arrets.Ganhi: Banks, shops and the Notre-Dame cathedral, striped red and white.
arrets.Akpakpa: The east bank of the lagoon, linked to the centre by three bridges.

arrets.Haie Vive: Restaurants, maquis and terraces: this is where Cotonou goes out at night.
arrets.Erevan: The junction with the Bio Guéra statue and the Erevan department store.
arrets.Palais des Congrès: The white drums inspired by the tata somba, opened in 2003.
arrets.Palais de la Marina: The Presidency of the Republic, facing the ocean.
arrets.Ganhi: Banks, shops and the cathedral of Notre-Dame de Miséricorde.

arrets.Carrefour Kpota: The big junction of Abomey-Calavi, where the pirogues leave for Ganvié.
arrets.UAC: The University of Abomey-Calavi, the largest in the country, founded in 1970.
arrets.IITA: The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture and its forest.
arrets.Échangeur de Godomey: The western gateway to Cotonou. Since 2021, the tokpa-tokpa minibuses stop here.

plage.nom: From the beach to the stadium

arrets.Plage de Fidjrossè: The western beach, along the Route des Pêches.
arrets.Fidjrossè: The neighbourhood of drinks stalls and coconut palms, between the airport and the sea.
arrets.Agla: A large residential neighbourhood in the north-west of the city.
arrets.Stade de l'Amitié: The Général Mathieu Kérékou stadium, in Kouhounou.
arrets.Étoile Rouge: The monument roundabout, in the heart of the city.

arrets.Temple des Pythons: The temple of Dangbé, the python god, facing the Basilica of the Immaculate Conception.
arrets.Place Chacha: The former auction square, where the Route des Esclaves begins, running nearly 4 km down to the sea.
arrets.Arbre de l'Oubli: Captives had to walk around it to forget their homeland: nine times for men, seven times for women.
arrets.Zoungbodji: The mass grave memorial and the Tree of Return, walked around so that the soul would one day come back.
arrets.Porte du Non-Retour: The memorial facing the ocean, at the end of the Route des Esclaves. Next to it, the Arène de Ouidah, home of the Vodun Days.

arrets.Ganhi: The business district, at the foot of the cathedral.
arrets.Akpakpa: The east bank, its markets and its workshops.
arrets.Corniche Est: The promenade along the Atlantic, with its jogging track and coconut palms.
arrets.Donaten: The Akpakpa seafront and its new villas.
